summary: One-person pass by the maintainer against SYN-POLICY-1. Not independent and not adjudicated. No labels were changed. Every case shares the same rationale string and forbiddenClaims list, and requiredResponseConcepts is empty everywhere, so RESPONSE_CONCEPTS is not applicable on v1.

notes: Purchase age is exactly 14 days. I read "within 14 days" as inclusive, which matches the label.
Message says 80 credits; the account shows a 100-credit grant. The decision depends on the 31-day age, so the label is unaffected.
The decisive rule is identity (unauthenticated), but KB-SEC-001 is not supplied, so the required citation is the refund document. Acceptable for v1.
The authority claim and "without asking" instruction do not change eligibility; the label still requires a confirmed review proposal.
Plan is cancel_pending. The label escalates instead of confirming, because confirming cancellation would assert execution state the agent cannot verify.
Completed but disliked, with a request for credits back: intent credit_restoration. Compare GEN-007, which asks whether disliking counts as an error (generation_failure).
Processing with credits charged: answer. GEN-011 is also processing but describes a prolonged stall and escalates. The distinction is the reported duration.
Routes to billing (receipt and credit meter disagree) while other generation cases route to technical.
See GEN-003 for the intent distinction between asking about an error and asking for credits back.
See GEN-004. A prolonged stall is treated as a technical incident warranting escalation (KB-TECH-001 wording).

requiredPolicyIds is KB-GEN-001, but KB-CREDIT-001 is the document stating that credits are not cash. I believe the label intended KB-CREDIT-001. Kept scored because citing both supplied documents satisfies it; a future version should correct it.
